raw_review_excerpt:
The plan is directionally sound and scoped with reasonable restraint, but it is not yet sufficiently anchored to repo reality: named files, workflow entrypoints, and amend/message-generation semantics are asserted in the artifact rather than verified against current code or docs.

Issues:
- 1. [WARN] Repo-pattern anchoring is missing for the named touchpoints
- 2. [WARN] A key semantic choice is still unresolved at plan time
- 3. [WARN] Trailer normalization may be less localized than the plan implies
- 4. [WARN] The mandatory-path goal is broader than the documented audit scope
- 5. [NOTE] The deferred `commit.verify-last` follow-on depends on an unproven policy contract

review.summary: The plan is directionally sound and scoped with reasonable restraint, but it is not yet sufficiently anchored to repo reality: named files, workflow entrypoints, and amend/message-generation semantics are asserted in the artifact rather than verified against current code or docs.

rubric_cards.title: Claim Anchoring
rubric_cards.claim: The artifact anchors its intended behaviors well, but its repo-specific claims are only partially grounded because concrete file paths and canonical-doc assumptions are not corroborated by inspected repo sources.
rubric_cards.evidence: Artifact steps 2, 3, and 8 name schema mirrors, `sdk/src/query/commit.ts`, and `get-shit-done/references/git-planning-commit.md`; no directly inspected local file evidence was available in this review.

rubric_cards.title: Disposition Matrix
rubric_cards.claim: The review can distinguish what is supported by the artifact text from what remains unverified about conversation history and broader campaign context.
rubric_cards.evidence: Only the supplied plan text and current prompt constraints were used; no prior-round packet, broader thread history, or repo files were inspected.

rubric_cards.title: Coverage Scope
rubric_cards.claim: This is a slice review of one plan artifact, not a full-campaign or repo-pattern validation.
rubric_cards.evidence: The review covered steps 1 through 9 of the supplied document and the stated focus, but not the actual implementation files, docs inventory, or surrounding workflow history.

conversation_evidence.summary: Conversation evidence was used only to bound scope and explain why repo-grounded verification is absent; it was not used to substantiate technical claims about the implementation plan.
gaps: No prior-round review packet was provided.
No earlier thread evidence was used to confirm repo history or workflow intent.
Conversation evidence does not replace missing code/doc inspection.

covered: Internal logic and sequencing of steps 1 through 9.
Risks visible from the artifact text around config, trailers, amend behavior, tests, and docs scope.
missing: Actual repo files and current implementation patterns.
Current SDK/config/test/doc entrypoints for commit behavior.
Broader campaign or thread history beyond this single review request.
Any prior-round packet or verified closure evidence.
gaps: Do not read this as a repo-grounded approval of the named paths or patterns.
The review does not establish that `gsd-sdk query commit` already controls every relevant workflow commit path.

issues.title: Repo-pattern anchoring is missing for the named touchpoints
issues.details: The plan names concrete schema mirrors, a specific SDK file, and a canonical doc path, but the review has no inspected evidence that these are the actual or complete touchpoints in the repo. That weakens feasibility confidence more than the artifact acknowledges.
issues.suggested_fix: Before execution, verify that the named files are canonical and sufficient for commit config, CLI parsing, and docs coverage.

issues.title: A key semantic choice is still unresolved at plan time
issues.details: Step 6 leaves amend behavior open between rejecting `--trailer` with `--amend --no-edit` and implementing message reconstruction. That is a load-bearing behavior choice because tests, UX, and edge-case handling all depend on it.
issues.suggested_fix: Resolve amend semantics from the current implementation and expected UX before treating the plan as execution-ready.

issues.title: Trailer normalization may be less localized than the plan implies
issues.details: Step 4 assumes exact-once trailer normalization can be added cleanly, but existing trailers, blank-line rules, multiple trailer keys, and CLI-plus-config merge order can create subtle message-construction behavior that may already live outside the obvious CLI parsing layer.
issues.suggested_fix: Validate the current message-construction path and acceptance examples before concluding the change is confined to the stated scope.

issues.title: The mandatory-path goal is broader than the documented audit scope
issues.details: The goal says `gsd-sdk query commit` should become the mandatory path for GSD workflow commits, but step 8 only references one canonical doc and some common workflow sections. That does not, by itself, show that all commit entrypoints and instructions are covered.
issues.suggested_fix: Inventory workflow entrypoints and commit guidance first so the mandatory-path claim is evaluated against the full surface, not a likely subset.

issues.title: The deferred `commit.verify-last` follow-on depends on an unproven policy contract
issues.details: Step 9 is disciplined about deferring scope, but it assumes last-commit-only verification can be isolated cleanly from broader git-state checks and that trailer policy will be crisp enough to verify deterministically after the first feature lands.
issues.suggested_fix: Keep this explicitly separate until trailer behavior and policy boundaries are proven by the first change set and its tests.

verification_gaps: No local repo files were inspected, so repo-pattern claims are unverified.
No test files or existing test helpers were inspected, so test-scope completeness is unknown.
No current CLI option parser behavior was inspected, so repeatable `--trailer` feasibility is inferred, not verified.
No current commit-message construction path was inspected, so normalization placement is inferred, not verified.
No workflow/docs inventory was inspected, so the mandatory-path objective may have uncovered surfaces.
review.best_case: If the named SDK/config/doc touchpoints are in fact canonical, this is a sensible incremental plan: it keeps scope narrow, preserves existing pathspec protections, forces an explicit amend decision, and defers `verify-last` until trailer support is proven.
strongest_objections: The plan makes repo-specific assertions about files, schema mirrors, and canonical docs without verified repo evidence.
The amend behavior decision is still open even though it drives acceptance criteria, test design, and user-facing semantics.
Exact-once trailer normalization is easy to describe but often subtle in practice once existing trailers, ordering, and blank-line rules are involved.
The goal of making `gsd-sdk query commit` mandatory across workflow commits is broader than the artifact's documented audit of entrypoints and docs.
hidden_assumptions: `gsd-sdk query commit` already sits on every relevant workflow commit path that matters to the goal.
The SDK and CJS schema mirrors named in the plan are the full set of config touchpoints that need parity updates.
Current commit-message construction is isolated enough that trailer normalization can be added without unexpected side effects.
Existing trailers can be preserved and deduplicated with a straightforward exact-once rule across both CLI and config sources.
The canonical documentation and workflow reminder surfaces are already known well enough that a narrow doc pass will close the behavioral gap.
review.what_would_change_my_mind: Inspecting the current commit query implementation, config schemas, tests, and commit-related docs and finding that the named files are canonical, the CLI already has a clean repeatable-flag pattern, message construction is centralized, and workflow entrypoints already converge on this one commit path would materially increase confidence.
next_checks: Confirm whether `sdk/src/query/commit.ts` is the actual single entrypoint for workflow commit creation or only one of several paths.
Inventory every config/schema mirror and docs-parity check that currently governs `commit.*` settings.
Inspect the existing commit-message builder to determine where trailer parsing, ordering, dedupe, and blank-line normalization actually belong.
Map workflow commands and docs that still invoke or recommend raw `git commit` so the mandatory-path goal has a verified surface area.
Decide amend semantics from current behavior and acceptance expectations before finalizing implementation or test scope.
